title: Frontend attachment flow: signed-URL upload/download components
objective: Update the SPA attachment components to the signed-URL envelope flow (request -> authorize/validate -> signed URL -> direct-to-storage transfer -> confirm), including progress and error states, while keeping validation UX (type/size messages) unchanged (A-7, M-25, spec 10 change 4).
scope: Upload component: call request-upload, PUT the file to the signed URL with progress, then confirm; render validation errors (type/size) exactly as before; handle signed-URL expiry and confirm failures with retry affordance
Download: call the download endpoint, navigate/fetch the signed URL (attachment disposition); error states for expired URLs
Remove flow unchanged against the soft-remove endpoint
API-client layer additions for the envelope DTOs
implementation_details: Use fetch/XHR PUT directly to the signed URL (bytes bypass /api/v1 and the Vercel body cap); do not attach the app bearer token to storage requests.
Progress states via upload progress events; keep existing design-system components for progress/error rendering.
10MB client-side pre-check mirrors the server cap for UX only (server remains authoritative).
Component tests (Vitest) for the new flow per spec 17 frontend row — the only new component tests required by the migration.

unit: Component tests: request->PUT->confirm sequencing; progress rendering; server 422 (type/size) rendered with unchanged messages; signed-URL failure path
integration: Manual/dev verification against local stack: 10MB file uploads successfully end-to-end (exceeds the 4.5MB function cap, proving the bypass)
e2e: Attachment upload/download Playwright coverage adapted in T-043

findings.summary: The task file's assumed file paths (features/quotes/attachments/UploadAttachment.tsx, AttachmentList.tsx, attachments/__tests__/upload-flow.test.tsx) do not exist; the SPA has a single AttachmentsSection.tsx and its co-located test. Implemented in the ACTUAL locations rather than inventing a new directory.
findings.detail: The migration SPA renders quote attachments from one component, src/ui/src/features/quotes/AttachmentsSection.tsx (mounted by QuoteDetailPanel.tsx), with its test at src/ui/src/features/quotes/__tests__/AttachmentsSection.test.tsx. There is no attachments/ subdirectory and no split Upload/List components. Creating the task file's speculative paths would have duplicated a component that already exists and left the real render path on the old multipart flow. The envelope orchestration and its dedicated behaviour tests were added as quotesApi.attachments.test.ts and api/client.signedUrl.test.ts alongside the existing convention. Recorded as a deviation from the task file's file list, not a scope change.

findings.summary: uploadToken from the request-upload envelope is not sent as a separate value on the direct PUT; the token is embedded in the fully-qualified uploadUrl (matching T-027's measured wire and its own integration test).
findings.detail: T-027 returns uploadUrl = Supabase createSignedUploadUrl's signedUrl (a fully-qualified https URL with the token already in the query string, asserted /^https?:\/\// in attachments.test.ts) plus uploadToken separately. T-027's OWN integration test transfers with fetch(envelope.uploadUrl, { method: 'PUT', headers: { 'content-type': ... }, body }) and never uses uploadToken. The SPA client (putFileToSignedUrl) does exactly that PUT — url, content-type header, raw bytes, NO app bearer token. uploadToken is kept on the DTO type for contract parity but is not needed for the direct PUT. This matches T-027 exactly; flagged only because the DTO carries a field the client does not consume.

history.message: Task generated by Planner from approved spec.md. Maps to A-7/Q-22 frontend pairing, M-25, spec 10 change 4.

SPA attachment flow migrated to the A-7 signed-URL envelope, FRONTEND ONLY (no backend/DB touched).

T-027 CONTRACT MATCHED (source of truth, read from the actual routes/schemas/errors, not designed):
  request-upload  POST /quotes/{id}/attachments  -> 202 AttachmentUploadEnvelopeDto { attachmentId, quoteId, fileName, contentType, uploadUrl, uploadToken, expiresInSeconds }; body { fileName, contentType, declaredSizeBytes }.
  direct transfer PUT envelope.uploadUrl with content-type header + raw bytes, NO app token (matches T-027's own integration transfer()).
  confirm         POST /attachments/{id}/confirm -> 201 QuoteAttachmentDto (server-observed sizeBytes; magic-number check here, R-8).
  download        GET /attachments/{id}          -> AttachmentDownloadEnvelopeDto { downloadUrl (attachment disposition), ... }; follow the URL.
  remove          DELETE /attachments/{id}       -> 204, UNCHANGED.
  Error codes surfaced via existing NormalizedError.title: ATTACHMENT_DISALLOWED_TYPE/OVER_SIZE_CAP (422 at request), ATTACHMENT_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH/OBJECT_MISSING (422 at confirm), ATTACHMENT_ALREADY_CONFIRMED (409). Client-side type pre-check message kept UNCHANGED (UX-only).

FILES CHANGED:
  src/ui/src/api/client.ts — added putFileToSignedUrl (XHR PUT, upload-progress events, no bearer token, rejects NormalizedError on 4xx/expiry/abort) and navigateToSignedUrl (anchor click for the disposition URL); REMOVED now-dead apiPostMultipart (apiGetBlob/triggerBrowserDownload kept — still used by exportsApi).
  src/ui/src/features/quotes/quotesApi.ts — added envelope DTOs + requestAttachmentUpload/confirmAttachmentUpload/getAttachmentDownloadEnvelope and the uploadAttachment (request->PUT->confirm) / downloadAttachment (envelope->navigate) orchestrators; removeAttachment unchanged.
  src/ui/src/features/quotes/AttachmentsSection.tsx — upload progress (percent + <progress>), retry affordance retaining the pending file on failure, download now follows the signed URL.

TESTS ADDED (test-first; RED observed 16 failed before impl):
  src/ui/src/features/quotes/__tests__/quotesApi.attachments.test.ts — drives the REAL orchestration (mocks only the client layer): request->PUT->confirm sequencing+ordering, PUT targets the server URL, derived content-type for empty File.type, PUT-fail => no confirm, confirm-422 propagates (not swallowed), onProgress forwarded, download navigates to server URL / rejects without navigating.
  src/ui/src/api/client.signedUrl.test.ts — putFileToSignedUrl via a fake XHR: PUT to url, content-type, NO authorization header, progress fractions, 400 (expiry) rejects, network error rejects; navigateToSignedUrl clicks an anchor at the URL.
  src/ui/src/features/quotes/__tests__/AttachmentsSection.test.tsx — rewritten to drive the flow: onUploaded on success, in-flight progress render, error+retry surfaces server message and re-attempts with the same file, download requests the envelope, closed-quote gating preserved.

FAILURE MODES (each tested + user-visible): signed-URL expiry mid-PUT -> putFileToSignedUrl rejects 4xx/0 -> error alert + Retry; confirm 422 magic-number -> uploadAttachment rejects, propagates -> error alert + Retry; PUT network failure -> reject -> error alert + Retry. Retry re-runs the whole envelope (fresh URL), which is the correct remedy for expiry and for a confirm-deleted object.

CONTRACT PARITY VERIFIED FIRST-HAND against T-027's actual routes/schemas/errors (not the task file's designed contract): read attachments.routes.ts, attachments.schemas.ts, attachments.errors.ts in full. POST /quotes/{id}/attachments -> 202 AttachmentUploadEnvelopeDto{attachmentId,quoteId,fileName,contentType,uploadUrl,uploadToken,expiresInSeconds}, body {fileName,contentType,declaredSizeBytes} - matches quotesApi.ts exactly, field for field. POST /attachments/{id}/confirm -> 201 QuoteAttachmentDto - matches. GET /attachments/{id} -> AttachmentDownloadEnvelopeDto{downloadUrl,...} - matches. DELETE /attachments/{id} -> 204 - unchanged, matches. Error codes: ATTACHMENT_DISALLOWED_TYPE/OVER_SIZE_CAP both 422 at request (attachments.errors.ts), ATTACHMENT_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH 422 and ATTACHMENT_OBJECT_MISSING 422 at confirm, ATTACHMENT_ALREADY_CONFIRMED 409 (not 422) at confirm - the SPA's history message correctly states 409 for already-confirmed, matching the real code exactly.

PUT-TO-STORAGE SECURITY PROPERTY VERIFIED BY READING client.ts: putFileToSignedUrl uses a fresh XMLHttpRequest with ONLY a Content-Type header set (xhr.setRequestHeader('Content-Type', ...)) — no Authorization header, no X-Tenant-Id — confirmed by the client.signedUrl.test.ts assertion `expect(xhr?.requestHeaders['authorization']).toBeUndefined()`. No app-token leak to the storage origin. Ruling: no security regression.

F-028-1 RULING: verified. AttachmentsSection.tsx (grep-confirmed as the sole render path, mounted by QuoteDetailPanel.tsx) is the real, pre-existing component location; the task file's speculative UploadAttachment.tsx/AttachmentList.tsx paths do not and never did exist. Building in the real location rather than a duplicate directory was correct. RESOLVED, no action needed.

F-028-2 RULING: verified against T-027's schemas.ts header comment and the adapter's own behavior — uploadUrl is the fully-qualified Supabase signed URL with the token embedded in the query string; uploadToken is a redundant field on the DTO (present because supabase-js's own uploadToSignedUrl helper takes it as a separate argument, an API the SPA does not use since it PUTs directly via XHR instead). Confirmed the client's PUT never needs a second token value. Not a bug: an unused-but-present DTO field, not a missing-but-required one. RESOLVED, no action needed.

FAILURE-MODE TESTS VERIFIED AS BEHAVIOR-DRIVEN, NOT RENDER-ONLY: read quotesApi.attachments.test.ts and client.signedUrl.test.ts in full. Confirmed real call-sequencing assertions: request->PUT->confirm ordering via invocationCallOrder, the PUT target asserted to be the ENVELOPE's server-returned uploadUrl (not hardcoded), PUT-fail => confirm never called (apiPost toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)), confirm-422 propagates via rejects.toBe (not swallowed), download rejects without navigating. AttachmentsSection.test.tsx additionally drives retry end-to-end: uploadAttachment mocked to fail once then succeed, Retry click re-invokes uploadAttachment a second time with the SAME File object (mock.calls[1][1] === file) - since uploadAttachment always starts from requestAttachmentUpload, this proves Retry re-runs the whole envelope with a fresh URL, the correct remedy for both mid-PUT expiry and a confirm-deleted object. Signed-URL expiry (400 from storage), confirm 422, and PUT network failure are each independently tested and each drives an error alert + Retry affordance in the component test.
